review_requirements.desired_state: Articulate the source-visible tower and stepped-wing elevations with a pale projecting structural grid, recessed glazing, aligned floor and bay divisions, transparent street-level frontage and the darker lower facade zone.
review_requirements.evidence: SOURCE shows repeated framed glazed bays on both visible tower faces and the stepped wing; CURRENT shows uninterrupted opaque faces.

review_requirements.desired_state: Form the source-visible setback terraces with connected surfaces, perimeter edges, recessed outdoor bays and planting zones, including those above the low wing; keep terrace slabs clear of adjoining enclosure walls.
review_requirements.evidence: SOURCE shows planted terrace edges and recessed outdoor spaces along the descending wing; CURRENT provides bare prism tops. Concealed roof geometry and internal joints remain uncertain.

review_requirements.desired_state: Add the source-visible neighboring building's repeated punched window rows, darker ground-floor openings and distinct vegetated far-right end-wall zone while preserving its position beside the tower.
review_requirements.evidence: SOURCE clearly differentiates the neighbor's windowed beige street facade and green end wall; CURRENT represents it as a blank beige block.

assessment: The source shows a street-level corner view of a glazed tower, an attached stepped wing descending left toward a low-rise end block, planted terraces, and a beige neighboring building with punched windows. Pale projecting facade grids, recessed glazing and transparent lower storeys define the main building. CURRENT preserves the broad arrangement but shows solid, unarticulated masses: openings, facade relief and terrace assemblies are missing. Rear elevations, hidden connections and exact dimensions are not established by the source; canonical views cannot prove their fidelity or joint construction.

issues.problem: The tower and stepped wing are opaque blue-grey blocks. Both source-visible tower faces and the wing lack the repeated pale structural grid, recessed window bays and glazed street-level frontage.
issues.action: Retain the existing mass arrangement and locally articulate the observed elevations with projecting frame members, recessed glazing and floor/bay divisions aligned across adjoining sections. Distinguish the darker lower facade zone shown in the source.

issues.problem: The stepped wing has bare block tops instead of the source-visible occupied terrace edges, planting zones and recessed outdoor bays. Its outline alone does not reproduce these spatial transitions.
issues.action: Locally form terrace surfaces, perimeter edges and recessed bays at the visible setbacks, including the planted terraces above the low wing. Connect these assemblies to the adjoining enclosure; avoid floating edges or slabs extending through walls. Infer concealed roof areas conservatively.

issues.problem: The beige neighboring building remains a blank prism. The source shows repeated punched windows, a darker open ground-floor frontage and a distinct vegetated far-right end wall.
issues.action: Articulate its source-visible street facade with the observed window rows and ground-floor openings, and distinguish the vegetated end-wall material zone. Preserve its existing position beside the tower.

keep: Tower placement at the right end of the ascending stepped frontage.
Flat roof form of the left low-rise end block.

issues.problem: The descending wing and low left wing have bare prism tops instead of the source-visible recessed outdoor bays, terrace edges and planting zones. Source-visible planted roof edges are also absent.
issues.action: Develop the existing setbacks locally into connected terrace surfaces with perimeter edges, recessed bays and contained planting. Keep slabs clear of adjoining enclosure walls; concealed roof layouts remain inferred.

issues.problem: The right neighbor remains a blank beige block, omitting its source-defining punched window rows, darker street-level openings and green far-right end wall.
issues.action: Add those visible envelope features to the existing neighbor, retaining its placement beside the tower.

Camera differences limit exact bay-width comparisons; concealed backing-wall openings and connections remain unverified.

review_requirements.desired_state: Form the source-visible setback terraces with connected surfaces, perimeter edges, recessed outdoor bays and planting zones, including those above the low wing; keep terrace slabs clear of adjoining enclosure walls.
review_requirements.evidence: Roof surfaces and planting rows now exist, so the earlier bare-prism description no longer applies. Current roof, left and street views still show simplified thin terrace edges rather than the source-visible depth of planted edges and recessed outdoor spaces. No definite slab penetration is established; concealed connections remain uncertain.

review_requirements.desired_state: Add the source-visible neighboring building's repeated punched window rows, darker ground-floor openings and distinct vegetated far-right end-wall zone while preserving its position beside the tower.
review_requirements.evidence: Window rows, dark ground-floor openings and a green end-wall zone are now present. The visible window columns remain excessively narrow and closely spaced relative to SOURCE, and the green wall lacks visible vegetation relief. Preserve the established adjacency and existing dark ground-floor treatment while correcting these remaining envelope differences.

assessment: SOURCE shows one street perspective: a gridded tower descending through planted setbacks toward a low connecting wing and left block, plus a beige neighboring building with punched windows and a vegetated far-right wall. Pale projecting members, recessed glazing and outdoor bays, and a darker lower facade zone define the visible architecture. CURRENT captures establish these broad relationships and now include facade grids, planting and neighbor openings, but their assemblies remain simplified. The current street camera exposes less of the tower’s right face, limiting dimensional comparisons. No confirmed dimensions are supplied; hidden elevations and concealed terrace connections remain uncertain. These screenshots do not establish a definite slab penetration or floating joint.

issues.problem: CURRENT reads as a nearly continuous blue glazed envelope with thin, heavily outlined divisions. SOURCE has a more substantial pale projecting grid, visibly recessed glazing and outdoor bays, and a distinct darker lower facade zone.
issues.action: Locally adjust the existing grid’s section, projection and finish; recess the appropriate glazing and outdoor bays, and articulate the source-visible lower facade zone while retaining correctly aligned divisions.

issues.problem: CURRENT adds planting rows and roof surfaces, but the setbacks and low-wing terraces still read primarily as thin roof edges. SOURCE shows deeper planted terrace edges and recessed outdoor spaces integrated with the facade.
issues.action: Develop the existing terraces’ visible perimeter edges, planting zones and recessed bays. Connect their surfaces to the adjoining facade assembly and verify slab terminations without inventing concealed roof arrangements.

issues.problem: The neighboring building now has openings, but CURRENT uses more tightly spaced, narrow window columns than SOURCE. Its far-right wall is a uniform green plane rather than the visibly vegetated envelope.
issues.action: Correct the visible window spacing and opening proportions locally, retain the dark ground-floor openings, and give the green end-wall zone visible vegetation depth and coverage.

keep: Right-hand placement of the beige neighboring building beside the tower.
Direction of the stepped descent from the tower toward the low connecting wing.

review_requirements.desired_state: Form the source-visible setback terraces with connected surfaces, perimeter edges, recessed outdoor bays and planting zones, including those above the low wing; keep terrace slabs clear of adjoining enclosure walls.
review_requirements.evidence: CURRENT 9–10 establishes substantial layered edges, guards and planting. The upper low-wing assemblies still appear as projecting trays against continuous glazing rather than SOURCE's staggered planted recesses. Correct terrace depth and adjoining enclosure locally. review_requirements.desired_state: Add the source-visible neighboring building's repeated punched window rows, darker ground-floor openings and distinct vegetated far-right end-wall zone while preserving its position beside the tower.
review_requirements.evidence: CURRENT 8–9 improves the small upper row and taller opening proportions, while retaining dark ground openings and the vegetated end wall. assessment: SOURCE shows one street-level oblique view: a gridded tower stepping down toward a connected low left wing, planted terraces and recessed outdoor bays, a darker lower facade zone, and a right neighbor with punched windows and a vegetated end wall. Street tracks establish the foreground orientation. CURRENT preserves these principal landmarks, but source-visible recess depth, low-wing terrace configuration and neighboring window-row organization remain mismatched. Rear elevations, complete roof layouts and concealed connections are unobserved in SOURCE; no dimensions are confirmed. The supplied captures establish no definite slab penetration or floating rail.

issues.problem: SOURCE’s outdoor openings occupy substantial recessed bays within the structural grid. CURRENT 8–9 still shows several as short horizontal slots or pale panels surrounded by glazing, flattening the tower elevations.
issues.action: Locally recess the affected bay infill and connect its floor, side returns and overhead enclosure. Retain the existing projecting grid members and glazing reveals elsewhere.

issues.problem: CURRENT 9–10 improves terrace edges and guards, but the upper assemblies read as projecting balcony trays against continuous glazing. SOURCE shows staggered planted recesses integrated into the stepped wing.
issues.action: Adjust the existing terrace depths and adjoining enclosure locally to form those recessed outdoor spaces. Preserve the improved perimeter edges where compatible; do not extrapolate the unseen roof plan.

issues.problem: CURRENT now has the small upper window row, but below it repeats six separate rows of tall rectangles. SOURCE shows fewer, taller vertically subdivided window groups, producing a different floor and opening rhythm.
issues.action: Regroup the existing lower openings into the source-visible taller assemblies with internal vertical articulation. Preserve the small upper row, dark ground openings and vegetated end wall.
